title: Answer: a sound argument that subjects cannot combine, or an intelligible physical account

statements.text: The view would be undercut by a sound argument that the combination problem cannot be solved, by an intelligible account of experience arising from the wholly non-experiential, or by a better-supported proposal for the intrinsic nature of matter. Goff grants that the combination problem may leave panpsychism no advance on physicalism.

sources.quote: It may turn out that the combination problem renders panpsychism no advance on physicalism, at least as regards explaining animal consciousness; time will tell.
